context:
Goal: the other-checkout guard stops refusing quoted text as a write, such as a read-only judge script given a quoted redirect to a parent folder as its argument.
Problem (rule): the fix check after round 3 found one hole main does not have: a kept script that runs a helper through a built path (`bash "$PWD/helper.sh"`, `bash $f`, `bash h*.sh`) leaves the helper's body unread. One hole opened and none closed, so the net safety value is negative, and your ruling parks the branch until you decide.
Based on (measured): the fix-check reviewer probed 8e8cf9232 against main: main refuses each built-path form and the branch allows it; 10 false-alarm forms are fixed.
Based on (read): the false alarm recurred 4 times today (3 test-author probes at 06:25 CST, triage at 07:00 CST), and once more when triage wrote this item (10:38 CST).
Departs from: main, where a quoted argument holding a write-looking token is refused on every interpreter command — the branch reads it as data when the script is in view and runs no shell.
Meanwhile: the lane takes #1984 through review round 3 and leaves this branch untouched.

options.gain: The false alarms close, and the branch opens no hole Claude could write by mistake.
options.how: A new lane from round 1 makes the guard keep every body when a kept body runs a path it cannot resolve (hooks/guard_core.py _kept_headers, the rule the outer scan already uses). Then a fix check, then it merges after #1906.
options.label: One fix lane for that hole
options.lose: One more lane, with up to 3 review rounds.

options.gain: No more work spent on it.
options.how: The branch stays held, with no more work.
options.label: Park the branch
options.lose: The false alarm stays on every probe or judge script that quotes a redirect.

short: Held guard fix: one more lane?
title: May the held quoted-text fix to the other-checkout guard get one more fix lane?
